title: Shoe the Horse
subject: A Midrand farrier can only fit a cart-horse's new shoes while a slow house track plays, because the old horse stamps in time and stands still
caption: South African kwaito-pop, slowed 1990s township house groove. Heavy kick and clap pattern, deep rounded sub bass, shaker running straight eighths, warm Rhodes-style piano stabs, a bright whistle melody on the hook. Warm wide mix with light hiss. Male lead voice, relaxed and bright, female group answering each line in call and response. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 108 BPM, F minor. Playful, loose, easy to dance to. No rapping, no autotune, no trap hi-hats, no guitars, no EDM drops, no orchestra.
lyrics:
[Intro - kick, shaker, Rhodes stabs]

[Verse 1]
Sunday at the stable, Midrand side
Old grey horse, he will not stand
I bring the hammer, I bring the nails
He wants the beat or he wants no part

[Pre-Chorus]
Press play, press play
Hold his foot, hold his foot

[Chorus]
Shoe the horse, shoe the horse
Hammer on the one
Ooh, he nods and he stays
Four new shoes by the end of the day

[Verse 2]
Left front foot on my leather apron
He stamps along with the bass
I file the hoof, I fit the iron

[Pre-Chorus]
Turn it up, turn it up

[Chorus]
Shoe the horse, shoe the horse
Hammer on the one
Ooh, the old horse stamps in time
Cart is waiting by the gate

[Outro - whistle, shaker, Rhodes]
Shoe the horse
One more foot
